newsitem.title: USA: US spot propane steady to higher in late trade.
newsitem.headline: US spot propane steady to higher in late trade.

text.p: U.S. spot propane prices were steady to higher in quiet activity late on Friday amid news of a minor pipeline leak and unconfirmed rumors of propane and butane being exported abroad, players said.
The Texas Eastern Transmission Company said late Friday it has shut down its 20-inch line from Texas to Indiana because of a minor leak.
The leak occurred Thursday in Stoddard County, Missouri, and is expected to delay deliveries for the next 24 to 48 hours, TET said.
A smaller line that runs parallel to the 20-inch pipeline has not been affected.
Meanwhile, several players were continuing to talk of unconfirmed rumors that propane and butane had been exported or diverted to Central America, which has helped to support U.S. prices.
In the Midwest, Conway, Kansas, hub spot propane rose 1.00 cent to between 77.50 cents and 78.00 cents a gallon. Wets were sold at 80.50 cents.
In the U.S. Gulf Coast, Mont Belvieu, Texas, spot propane largely held steady at 67.00/67.50 cents.
Most of the focus today, and much of the week, has been on propane, traders said.
-- Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1631
